steps.description:
You will be creating a program to simulate 2 exploring characters: Roamer and Hunter. They travel on a 10 rows by 20 columns field which is marked randomly with "X". Below shows an example of how it looks like (Roamer and Hunter are indicated by "R" and "H" respectively)

You will be creating 3 python classes to represent Roamer, Hunter and the Field. For this part of the project, we'll focus on creating the Field.

Write a class named Field with a 2D list variable field to represent a field 10 rows by 20 columns. When instanced, 40 objects (marked as "X") will be placed randomly in the field except at the edges. The rest of the cells will contain ".". Field has a function display() which clears the screen, display field and pause for 0.5 seconds.

Field also contains a static function main(), which runs the simulation. At this step, main() will just create an object of Field and run its display() function.

Run the code Field.main()

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Your result may vary due to random generator

This part of the project will focus on Roamer. Continue your program from the previous step.

Roamer travels randomly on the field one step at a time (up, down, left or right). When it encounters an "X", it will change direction to avoid stepping onto it. Write a class Roamer with the following attributes:

Object Variables row, col to store its position in the field using row and column indices. Roamer is marked by "R" in the field and begins at 0,0.

Function navigate(field) takes in the Field object to navigate.

Each time Roamer's navigate(field) is called, it will do the following: 1. It will generate the next direction of move randomly (up, down, left or right). 2. It will move one step in the direction only if it is within the field range and it is an empty space ".". 3. It will repeat step (1) to (2) until it has successfully moved a step.

Modify Field.main() as follow: 1. Create an object of Field and Roamer. 2. Initialise field[0][0] to "R". 3. Navigate Roamer one step. 4. Update display. 5. Repeat step (3) to (4) repeatedly.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Your result may vary due to random generator: Sample snapshots of field display. R is moving randomly while avoiding X.

This part of the project will focus on Hunter. Continue your program from the previous step.

Write another class called Hunter. Hunter is marked by "H" and begins at 9,19. It also has a navigate(field) function but with different conditions (your may choose to inherit Roamer and override navigate depending on your implementation)

Each time Hunter's navigate(field) is called, it will do the following: 1. It will generate the next direction of move randomly (up, down, left or right). 2. It will move one step in the direction only if it is within the field range. It can step on "X". The "X" will then disappear and become ".". 3. It will repeat step (1) to (2) until it has successfully moved a step.

Modify Field.main() as follow: 1. Create an object of Field, Roamer and Hunter. 2. Navigate Roamer one step 3. Navigate Hunter one step. 4. Update display. 5. Repeat step (2) to (4) repeatedly until Hunter steps on Roamer

You may add more variables or functions where required.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Have Fun with Characters (optional)

You can try this out for fun when your codes are working. Replace your charcters with emojis from this site for fun (modify your display function): https://unicode.org/emoji/charts/full-emoji-list.html

Try to use characters from the same group so that they have the same size to avoid distortion. The test output shows a sample using the the following characters (you may copy and paste the character into your code): Roamer 🌞 Hunter 🌛 X 🪐 . 🌚

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Your result may vary due to random generator: Sample snapshots of field display. R and H are moving randomly.

R meets H

Object Variables row, col to store its position in the field using row and column indices. Roamer is marked by "R" in the field and begins at 0,0. direction stores the last direction moved: 1 - Up / 2 - Down / 3 - Left / 4 - Right It is initialised to 1.

It will move one step in the direction only if it is within the field range and it is an empty space ".". 3. It will repeat step (1) to (2) until it has successfully moved a step.

Each time Hunter's navigate(field) is called, it will do the following: 1. If there is a neighbouring "X" or "R" (above, below, left or right), it step onto it. 2. If there is not, it will navigate as follow: a. use random number to generate 20% chance of changing direction. If it hits the 20% chance, it will randomly generate the next direction of move (1 to 4, excluding last direction), otherwise it will keep to the last direction. b. it will move one step in the direction if it is within the field range. c. it will repeat step (a) to (b) until it has successfully moved a step.
